audit_findings.title: Antares completion breaks the perimeter and equity-interest coherence
audit_findings.mechanism: The OE anchor excludes controlled Antares operations and post-close financing costs, while the bridge uses the post-close $1,453.9 million debt balance.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company accounts for its investment in Antares Vision in the first phase under equity method accounting since it exercises significant influence over Antares Vision, but does not have a controlling financial interest.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated timing and perimeter mismatch, not merely a possible risk. The September valuation capitalizes pre-control 2025 owner earnings but uses a June 2026 balance sheet after the $417.1 million acquisition. Antares contributed $63.7 million of second-quarter sales and a $5.4 million operating loss, while acquisition financing increased interest expense. Those figures do not establish normalized owner earnings, but the omitted business and financing are large enough reasonably to change the valuation. The direction is mixed because Antares adds operating cash generation while interest, integration costs, NCI and ITT claims reduce value.
audit_findings.action: Recompute trailing post-close owner earnings using consolidated Antares results, recurring integration costs, acquisition interest, maintenance capex, working-capital needs, NCI and ITT claims; then rerun all scenarios with the same June 2026 balance sheet.

audit_findings.title: ITT performance shares create a separate claim ahead of CXT common
audit_findings.magnitude: $36.3 million filed liability at 2026-06-30 ($0.61 per CXT share computed); ultimate settlement unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The liability-classified subsidiary performance shares are a claim on value ahead of CXT common and should enter the equity bridge; remeasurement expense or benefit can also affect OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Once converted to ordinary shares, the Class B shares are subject to immediately exercisable call and put features and as such, they are liability-classified instruments.
audit_findings.explanation: A current claim is demonstrated: the June filing reports a $36.3 million Class B liability that is absent from the bridge. Deducting that amount alone would reduce base value from $36.85 to approximately $36.24 per share, which would not reverse the conclusion relative to the $50.06 price. Materiality remains unresolved because the conversion multiplier ranges from zero to three, the liability is remeasured each period and the eventual put or call settlement is not established by the record.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile all 3,635,104 Class B shares, expected conversion multiplier, June fair value, put and call terms, settlement funding and tax effects; deduct the resulting common-equity claim and normalize related remeasurement effects in OE.

audit_findings.title: The anchor contains only a partial year of DLR
audit_findings.magnitude: owner-earnings impact unquantified; DLR contributed $89.4 million of sales and a $7.9 million operating loss after acquisition, while filed 2025 pro forma net income was $160.3 million versus $145.1 million actual, a computed $15.2 million difference
audit_findings.mechanism: The partial-year acquisition results and financing distort the recurring OE anchor used for every forecast year.
audit_findings.evidence: DLR results of operations have been included in our financial statements for the period subsequent to the completion of the acquisition on May 1, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The non-comparable period is demonstrated, but its effect on owner earnings is unresolved. Eight months omit four months of DLR operations and associated cash economics, while reported operating loss includes acquisition amortization, fair-value step-up and transaction costs; a full year also entails additional interest. The filed pro forma net-income difference is meaningful but cannot be substituted directly for owner earnings, so the record cannot establish the net valuation impact or direction.
audit_findings.action: Construct a January-to-December 2025 same-perimeter DLR OE bridge from the pro forma disclosures, including full-year interest, taxes, maintenance capex and working capital while separately identifying purchase-accounting and genuinely nonrecurring costs; rerun the scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition costs are perpetuated without acquisition earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $24.1 million filed 2025 expense, equal to 17.3% of the $139.4 million OE anchor; comparable filed expenses were $19.9 million in 2024 and $22.0 million in 2023
audit_findings.mechanism: Retaining transaction costs in the anchor lowers recurring OE and every forecast cash flow despite growth scenarios that include no corresponding future acquired earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: We incurred transaction related expenses of $24.1 million, $19.9 million and $22.0 million for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively, recorded in “Selling, general and administrative” in the Consolidated and Combined Statements of Operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The expense burden is demonstrated, but inappropriate perpetuation is not: three consecutive years of similar costs and the stated acquisition strategy indicate that some normalized acquisition budget may be recurring. Conversely, retaining the entire $24.1 million while projecting only same-business growth understates value. Its pretax scale is significant relative to the anchor, but the recurring amount, tax effect and associated future acquisition returns are not established.
audit_findings.action: Separate separation costs from acquisition costs, identify costs tied to completed transactions, set an evidence-based recurring acquisition budget consistent with each scenario and rerun OE without adding acquisition earnings unless those earnings and purchase funding are modeled consistently.

audit_findings.title: Separation tax exposure is an unmodeled contingent senior claim
audit_findings.mechanism: If triggered, the tax liability would be deducted in the equity bridge or reduce OE through taxes and cash payments ahead of common shareholders.
audit_findings.evidence: If the distribution or any of the above referenced related transactions is determined to be taxable for U.S. federal income tax purposes, we could incur significant U.S. federal income tax liabilities.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes a forward-looking contingent exposure, not a present assessment or demonstrated valuation omission. The June 2026 filing reports $7.1 million of gross unrecognized tax benefits, but that amount does not quantify the potentially larger separation-disqualification exposure. Without evidence that representations or covenants were breached, the tail claim is not presently measurable and should be monitored rather than inserted as a speculative liability.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the IRS ruling, tax opinion, Tax Matters Agreement allocation, covenant-compliance evidence, indemnification terms and Crane Company's ability to perform; rerun the bridge if a breach, assessment, reserve or estimable exposure emerges.

audit_findings.title: The share denominator may double-count stale maximum awards
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum computed denominator excess of 1.876223 million shares; removing all of it would raise base value from $36.85 to about $38.05 and bull value from $40.69 to about $42.03
audit_findings.mechanism: Stale or duplicated awards overstate fully diluted shares and therefore understate per-share value; total equity value and OE are unchanged.
audit_findings.evidence: If the PRSUs included in this total vest at the target performance level as opposed to the maximum level, the aggregate awards outstanding would be 1,689,780.
audit_findings.explanation: Double-counting is an unresolved possibility, but even the conservative assumption that the entire difference between the 59.437527 million denominator and 57.561304 million July outstanding shares is erroneous would change per-share values by only about 3.3%. Bull value would remain approximately $8.03 below the $50.06 market price, and the buy-below level would rise only from $25.79 to about $26.63. It therefore cannot change the valuation conclusion on the supplied numbers.
audit_findings.action: Roll options, RSUs, DSUs and PRSUs from December 31, 2025 through July 31, 2026; remove vested, exercised, forfeited or already issued awards and apply documented performance outcomes before publishing the final per-share figures.
